title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction: Context: a digression in the continuation of La Longue Marche (ms. p. 769) on coverings of germs of spaces. A germ is a pair (S,Φ): a topological space S with a proper filter Φ. The previous page sets Rev(S,Φ) = 2-colim_{S_i∈Φ} Rev(S_i). This page first finishes a sentence from the previous page. Rev(S,Φ) is to be viewed as the category of coverings of a suitable topos, namely the projective limit of the small étale topoi of the S_i ∈ Φ, a pro-topos or 'germ topos'. 'In good cases' this category is multigaloisian, or even galoisian. Definition: (S,Φ) is 1-connected (simply connected) if the constant-covering functor (Ens) → Rev(S,Φ), E ↦ E_{(S,Φ)}, is an equivalence. This splits into two conditions. (1) Full faithfulness, called 0-connectedness ('connected' in the margin). For S locally connected this means: for every S_i ∈ Φ there is a nonempty S_j ⊂ S_i in Φ with π0(S_j) → π0(S_i) constant. (2) Essential surjectivity. This means: for every S_i there is S_j ⊂ S_i in Φ such that, for every connected component S_{j,α}, the canonical map π1(S_{j,α}) → π1(S_i) is trivial. Coverings of germs then form a fibred category over the category of germs. Ordinary spaces embed fully as germs with the trivial filter. On the next page this yields a fibre functor Rev(X) → Rev(S) ≃ Ens for any morphism S → X from a 1-connected germ S. This defines π1(X,S), a fundamental group based at a simply connected germ rather than at a point, with the Galois equivalence Rev(X) ≃ π-Ens. Typical uses are germs at infinity or at a puncture, e.g. sectors. This gives 'tangential' or 'germ' base points, and also a π1 at infinity / ends of a space.
errors: Condition 1° is correct (test with E = 1 and F a large set to force constancy). Nonemptiness of S_j is needed and was added by Grothendieck; this matches excluding the improper filter.

Condition 2° is sloppy. π1 needs base points, and the map should land in π1 of the component of S_i containing S_{j,α}. As a characterisation of essential surjectivity it is sufficient, and necessary only under local hypotheses on the S_i (locally path-connected, semi-locally simply connected). For general spaces, coverings only detect a completion of π1. It also relies on 1° to make the fibres constant across components.
The identification of Rev(S,Φ) with coverings of the limit topos is hedged ('dans les bons cas'). Commuting coverings with filtered limits of topoi needs finiteness or local-connectedness hypotheses.

missed.claim: Grothendieck's general device of basing fundamental groups at 1-connected germs (filters of neighbourhoods, e.g. sectors at a puncture) predates and generalises Deligne's tangential base points. It is set up purely topologically and topos-theoretically, as a fibred category of coverings over germs.
missed.quote: On dit qu'un germe d'espaces est 1-connexe, ou simplement connexe, si le foncteur naturel (Ens) → Rev(S,Φ) ... est une équivalence de catégories
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is relevant to the attribution history of tangential base points in Grothendieck–Teichmüller theory. It also offers a uniform 'germ' formalism for base points at infinity in étale homotopy.

missed.claim: The margin note suggests Grothendieck thought this germ/topos formalism had been worked out by Olivier Leroy (Montpellier), presumably in his work on the fundamental groupoid and van Kampen in topos theory.
missed.quote: cela a été fait par Olivier Leroy ?
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a historical pointer to under-cited Montpellier work linked to the Longue Marche programme.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics on this page is standard covering/shape theory for germs. The mild interest lies in where it leads: a general formalism of simply connected germs as base points (tangential base points avant la lettre), plus the margin reference to Olivier Leroy.
transcription_corrections: 'groupe d'espaces' should read 'germe d'espaces' throughout (both in the body and the margin).
The filter symbol is Φ, as on the previous page, not 𝔏.
Top-left margin: 'cela a été fait par Olivier Leroy ?' (not 'cela a fait').
'769' is the manuscript page number; '(petits)' is an insertion before 'topos étales'.
Second margin note: 'dans ce cas on dira que ce germe d'espaces est connexe'.
On the next page 'genres d'espaces' should read 'germes d'espaces'.
